clue.text: Understand mantra uttered by patriarch without hesitation

indicators.note: without means the hesitation sound is dropped from the patriarch word

parts.note: a patriarch is the father of a family
ER is the sound of hesitation
OM is the sacred syllable chanted as a mantra

explanation.surface: Someone tries to grasp the chant a holy elder recites smoothly, without stumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' leaves FATH; 'hesitation' is the crossword convention for the sound er.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to get to the bottom of it, i.e. to comprehend it.

clue.text: Emergency transport facility offered to skiers, excluding Switzerland

indicators.note: excluding means the letters for Switzerland are left out of the ski facility

parts.note: a chairlift carries skiers up the slope
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A ski resort's lift offered everywhere but in Switzerland, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluding' takes CH from CHAIRLIFT. The definition is only the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An airlift is the movement of people or supplies by aircraft, typically in a crisis.

clue.text: Hard politician taken in by American projections

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: taken in by means the politician sits inside the letters for American

parts.note: US means American
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A tough politician is fooled by an American's forecasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projections' looks like forecasts but means bulges.
explanation.definitionFit: Humps are rounded protrusions, things that stick out from a surface.

clue.text: Stories of my religious studies must omit Spain

indicators.note: must omit means the Spain letter has to come out of the subject

parts.note: theology is the study of religion
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A student complains their religious studies course has to leave Spain out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must omit' leaves THOLOGY.
explanation.definitionFit: A mythology is a body of traditional tales, so the word stands for a set of stories.

clue.text: Pleasure entertaining students with low night light?

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a host would, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: fun is pleasure
L is a learner, so LL is two students
to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Fun is had with students and a mooing cow under the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'low' is the cow's noise, not 'not high'; 'entertaining' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A full moon is the moon's fully lit phase, the brightest natural lamp of the night sky.

clue.text: Agents found in most of artificial treatments

indicators.note: found in means the agents are placed within the other piece
most of means the last letter is cut from the synonym

parts.note: false means artificial, as in false teeth
the CIA is the US intelligence agency, a body of agents

explanation.surface: Spies are discovered in most artificial cosmetic treatments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' gives FALS, which the agents are 'found in'. The clue word seems to conceal the answer but does not.
explanation.definitionFit: Facials are beauty treatments applied to the face.

clue.text: Hang around with no good way of going overseas

indicators.note: with no means the good letter is taken away from the verb

parts.note: to linger is to hang around

explanation.surface: Loitering is pointless when you need a route abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes G from LINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean liner is a passenger ship, a means of crossing the sea to another country.

clue.text: Disorder in market — there's mounting feeling

indicators.note: in means the reversed feeling word sits inside the market word

parts.note: a mart is a market

indicators.note: mounting means climbing, so in a down answer the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: sense means feeling

explanation.surface: Chaos in the market as sentiment grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns SENSE into ESNES, which goes 'in' MART. A mare's nest is a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare's nest is a complicated, confused state of affairs, a mess.

clue.text: Peanut possibly produced by poor soil on river flowing north

indicators.note: poor suggests the soil letters are in bad shape, so they are rearranged
flowing north in a down answer means the river's name reads upwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: A peanut crop grown in poor soil by a north-flowing river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' makes OILS from SOIL; 'flowing north' turns DEE into EED.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut is one example of a seed grown for its oil, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Cold Tory detailed offensive poster's device

parts.note: remote means cold or aloof
CON is short for Conservative, i.e. Tory

indicators.note: detailed means de-tailed, the last letter cut off

parts.note: a troll posts offensive things online

explanation.surface: An aloof Conservative describes an internet troll's gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is de-tailed, leaving TROL.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote control is a handheld gadget for operating a television or other apparatus at a distance.

clue.text: Rumoured returns mostly left on adult spread

indicators.note: returns means the word goes back the way it came, read right to left

parts.note: said means rumoured, as in 'he is said to be rich'

indicators.note: mostly means the synonym loses its last letter

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Gossip comes back, largely ignored, about a grown-up's flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns SAID into DIAS; 'mostly' trims PORT to POR. PORT is the nautical left.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is a people dispersed from their homeland, i.e. a scattering.

clue.text: Spoke harshly as understood golf cancelled

indicators.note: cancelled means the golf letter is struck out

parts.note: grasped means understood
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone snapped once they learned the golf match was off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cancelled' takes G from GRASPED.
explanation.definitionFit: To rasp is to say something in a grating, rough voice.

clue.text: Academic wanting you and I to find artist's place

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the pronoun's letters are taken away

parts.note: studious means academic, bookish
you and I together are us

explanation.surface: A scholar needs the two of us to track down a painter's workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' removes US from STUDIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is the room where a painter or sculptor works.

clue.text: Spiritual leader could be a country boy raised outside area

indicators.note: outside means the raised string goes around the area letter
raised means lifted up, so in a down answer the pieces read upwards

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A rural lad brought up somewhere might become a spiritual guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses the down string into DALILAMA, which then goes 'outside' A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the chief monk and spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: Follows top players outside university chapters

indicators.note: outside means the top players go around the other letters

parts.note: seeds are the top-ranked players in a tournament
C is chapter, so CC is chapters

explanation.surface: Tennis seeds training outside the university, with some chapters to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' is the containment signal; 'top players' are tournament seeds, not a first-letter instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed someone is to come after them in a post, i.e. to follow them.

clue.text: Sees bad rust in features found in road

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters sit inside the road features

parts.note: traffic cones are set out on roads

indicators.note: bad suggests the rust letters are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A motorist spots rust on the cones set out along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' turns RUST into STRU, which goes 'in' CONES.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe is to interpret or understand something a particular way, as 'I see it'.

clue.text: Cut across line and discussed terms for peace

indicators.note: across means the cut word spans the line, going round it

parts.note: pared means cut or trimmed
a ley line is supposed alignment of ancient sites, so ley means line

explanation.surface: Two sides cut across a boundary and then talked peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' is the containment signal; a ley line is a supposed alignment of ancient sites.
explanation.definitionFit: To parley is to hold talks with an enemy, typically to agree a truce.

clue.text: What may be read from reported traffic congestion?

indicators.note: reported means the phrase is as said aloud, so the spelling changes

parts.note: a queue of autos (cars) is traffic congestion

explanation.surface: What could you learn from news of a traffic jam?
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' turns 'auto queue', a line of cars, into the device's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocue is the screen a presenter reads a script from on television.

clue.text: Blooming Germany did what the Pied Piper did!

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

parts.words: did what the Pied Piper did
parts.note: the Pied Piper rid Hamelin of rats, so he ratted

explanation.surface: Germany is credited with the Pied Piper's feat, a nod to Hamelin's legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' is not about flowers: it is a mild British curse word, as is 'dratted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild expletives meaning confounded, used to express irritation.

clue.text: Yankee after rejecting suitable working brief

indicators.note: after means the Yankee letter comes at the end
rejecting means throwing back, so the two words read right to left

parts.note: fit means suitable
on means working, as a machine is
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American is turned down for a suitable job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' gives NOTIF and 'after' places Yankee last. 'Brief' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To brief someone is to inform them, give them the facts.

clue.text: Hotel is in luck — maids regularly ignored fool

indicators.note: is in means the hotel letter sits inside the luck word

parts.note: fate means fortune or luck
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter is skipped

explanation.surface: A hotel gets lucky though its maids are routinely overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' is the containment signal; 'regularly ignored' leaves the second and fourth letters of the maids word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fathead is a stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Faithful worshippers ultimately cheated, we hear

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the worshippers word
we hear means the word is as it sounds, not as spelt

parts.note: tricked means cheated

explanation.surface: Devout churchgoers were in the end swindled, it's said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives S; 'we hear' turns TRICKED into the sound TRICT.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict here means rigorously observant, as a strict believer is devout and loyal.

clue.text: Stunner — she loses heart, being pinched by sailor

indicators.note: being pinched by means held tight inside the sailor word

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: loses heart means the middle letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A beauty loses her nerve when a sailor gets fresh with her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' leaves SE, which is 'being pinched by' the old word for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A taser is an electric weapon used to stun people, hence a stunner.

clue.text: Remedy offered by a new spot in draw

indicators.note: in means the spot letters sit inside the draw word

parts.note: a tie is a drawn match
a dot is a spot

explanation.surface: A cure offered by a fresh blemish in the lottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like a lottery but is a tied match; 'in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote counteracts a poison, so it is a cure or remedy.

clue.text: Tail, then vanish out of sight

parts.note: to dog is to follow or tail someone
to go is to vanish, as in 'the pain has gone'

explanation.surface: A spy follows a target and then disappears from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie doggo' is British slang for keeping hidden and still.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggo, in 'lie doggo', means in hiding, keeping quiet and unseen.

clue.text: Pupils contest theory of marks, reportedly

parts.note: a class is a group of pupils
a struggle is a contest or fight

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren compete over how exams are graded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marks, reportedly' is spoken Marx: the class struggle is central to Marxist theory. 'Marks' looks like exam grades.
explanation.definitionFit: Class struggle, the conflict between social classes, is the core idea of Karl Marx's political theory.

clue.text: Retired couple beset by ruminants on the way back

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the couple goes inside
on the way back means the ruminants word reads in reverse

parts.note: deer are cud-chewing animals, ruminants
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: An elderly couple hemmed in by deer while walking home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' gives REED, by which the couple is 'beset'. 'Retired' means withdrew, not stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is a formal phrase for going or withdrawing there, as to retire to a room.

clue.text: Hesitant to accept strange material

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the strange word goes inside

parts.note: shy means hesitant or wary
odd means strange

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to accept unfamiliar fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' is the containment signal. Shoddy is the noun here, a recycled-wool cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy is a cloth made from recycled wool, a cheap material that gave the adjective its sense.
